title: And it begins...(a good start...) - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Morgan Stanley and Citigroup are pressuring large law firms to cut fees and switch to bid-based pricing, arguing AI has cut the hours needed per legal matter and should compress law-firm revenue per transaction — a trend Cowen says he predicted.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley and Citigroup have told major law firms they want new payment arrangements to save money, arguing that the billable-hour business model that has enriched top lawyers for decades is unsustainable in an era of AI.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Corporate legal spend is a major cost line for banks; if clients successfully force AI-adjusted fee cuts, large law firm revenue growth could stall even as billable hours needed per matter fall.
insights.quote: Wall Street banks are pushing large law firms to cut fees, arguing that the business model that has enriched top lawyers for decades is not sustainable in an era of AI.

insights.claim: Citigroup's global head of legal, Adam Meshel, said the bank now expects per-transaction legal costs to come down significantly when AI reduces the hours firms spend on a matter, and Citigroup has begun asking law firms to bid for work while disclosing how much they are saving by using AI.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A shift to competitive bidding tied to disclosed AI savings could become a template other large corporate clients replicate across professional services (consulting, accounting), pressuring margins industry-wide.
insights.quote: If the number of hours they're working on a matter has come down because of AI . . . our expectation is for costs to come down significantly per transaction.

insights.claim: Citigroup's Meshel described AI-driven efficiency gains as potentially causing a fundamental alteration of the revenue foundation for mega law firms.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Signals a structural repricing risk for elite law firm partnerships' revenue-per-partner model, a bellwether for how AI reshapes high-margin knowledge-work industries more broadly.
insights.quote: a fundamental altering of the revenue foundation for these mega firms

insights.claim: Cowen states he has been predicting this dynamic (banks forcing AI-driven fee compression on law firms) in many of his talks, positioning it as an early, real-world confirmation of a broader thesis that AI will compress fees across white-collar professional services.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Investors should watch for similar fee-compression moves spreading from legal to accounting, consulting, and investment banking as clients gain leverage from AI cost transparency.
insights.quote: I have been predicting exactly this in many of my talks…
